title: MethylPipeline User Manual
text:
1.1 What this manual is
This is the operational companion to the theory book. It is designed for execution teams who need:

exact commands,
required config keys,
expected output artifacts,
stage handoff checks,
recovery actions when a run fails.

For statistical background, use docs/theory/.

Daily operations: Chapters 10 to 12.

title: 4  Sample Prep and Quality Control
text:
4.1 Purpose
SamplePrepPipeline is the per-sample upstream workflow that turns raw WGBS FASTQs into methylation HDF5 files ({chromosome}-CG.h5) that downstream stages consume. Every sample passes through two automated guardrails before it enters stability, freeze, or discovery workflows:
Without these gates, bad alignments would waste GPU extraction time, and under-covered or poorly converted extractions would pollute centroids, DMP discovery, and classifiers.
Workflow source of truth: workflow_engine/domain/fixtures/sample_prep.program.json
Operator reference: workflow_engine/sql/SamplePrepFlow.md
crumbs: Part I: Setup and Package Orientation
4  Sample Prep and Quality Control

title: 4  Sample Prep and Quality Control
text:
Alignment QC (methyl-qc) — confirms Parabricks alignment and sequencing metrics are acceptable (or fixable via trim/realign).
Extraction QC (methyl-extraction-qc) — confirms MethylExtractor produced sufficient coverage and conversion-quality signal across chromosomes.
crumbs: Part I: Setup and Package Orientation

Gate
Scope variable
When
Blocks




Alignment
qcPass

Extraction

Ordering rationale: alignment QC runs before cfDNA fragmentomics so failed samples skip BAM scanning. Fragmentomics and extraction both need the aligned BAM. FASTQs are retained until QC is fully resolved so fastp can trim and Parabricks can realign on the remediation path.

title: 4  Sample Prep and Quality Control
section: 4.4 Alignment QC: inputs and normalized JSON
text:
4.4 Alignment QC: inputs and normalized JSON
methyl-qc (packages/methylalignmentqc) combines two upstream metric families into one decision:

4.4.1 Picard-style duplication metrics
Parabricks emits a tab-separated deduplication metrics file (names vary: *deduplicate_metrics.txt or *duplication_metrics.txt). The parser (methyl_alignment_qc/core/parser.py) reads Picard-compatible columns such as:

LIBRARY, UNPAIRED_READS_EXAMINED, READ_PAIRS_EXAMINED
SECONDARY_OR_SUPPLEMENTARY_RDS, UNMAPPED_READS
UNPAIRED_READ_DUPLICATES, READ_PAIR_DUPLICATES
PERCENT_DUPLICATION

These feed summary_stats on the export JSON (total reads, duplication rate, etc.). Optional config guardrails (step_config.alignment_qc.optional_guardrails.duplication_rate_max) can fail samples with excessive PCR duplication even when cycle quality looks fine.


4.4.2 Parabricks WGBS metrics JSON
Each sample directory should contain {sample_id}.json: Parabricks’ structured report with sections such as:

quality_yield — total/PF reads and Q30 bases
mean_quality_by_cycle — per-cycle mean Phred (Read 1 then Read 2; for 151+151 cycles, Read 2 starts at cycle 152)
gc_bias_summary, insert_size_metrics
pre_adapter_summaries — deamination and OxoG artifact qscores

When this file is present, guardrails in wgbs_parabricks_qc.py evaluate sequencing and alignment health before methylation extraction.


4.4.3 Our equivalent export JSON (V2)
The worker writes a normalized V2 row-oriented JSON per sample (schema: schemas/config/alignment_qc/exported_sample_qc_v2.schema.json). Key blocks:







Block
Contents




summary_stats
Duplication rate, read counts from Picard metrics


quality_yield, mean_quality_by_cycle, …
Parabricks sections (embedded or referenced)


guardrails.details
Per-metric pass/fail, observed value, normal range, operator message


guardrails.screening
Cycle-quality disposition and recommended trim counts


guardrails.overall_pass
Single boolean bound to workflow qcPass


qc_history
Append-only list of evaluations (initial + post-remediation retries)


fragmentomics_metrics
cfDNA insert-size guardrails when enabled



V1-shaped payloads are assembled internally and converted to V2 for export; standalone tools can migrate older files with methyl-qc-migrate-guardrails.
crumbs: Part I: Setup and Package Orientation
4  Sample Prep and Quality Control

title: 4  Sample Prep and Quality Control
text:
4.5 Alignment guardrails: what “good alignment” means
Core WGBS guardrails (defaults in wgbs_parabricks_qc.py) include:



Metric
Default expectation
Why it matters




PF read percent
≥ 90%
Run-level filtering quality


Q30 percent
≥ 85% (configurable)
Base-call confidence


Mean quality
≥ 35
Overall sequencing noise


Min quality after cycle 20
≥ 30
Late-cycle degradation


AT / GC dropout
< 3 / < 5
Coverage bias across genome


Median insert size
150–300 bp
Library fragmentation sanity


Deamination qscore
≤ 30
Expected WGBS conversion signal


OxoG qscore
≥ 20
Oxidative damage risk



Each metric carries a message explaining the biological/operational concern. guardrails.overall_pass is the logical AND of all evaluated checks (including optional and analyte-specific add-ons).

4.5.1 Optional and analyte-specific checks
Configure under step_config.alignment_qc in the project JSON:
{
  "alignment_qc": {
    "optional_guardrails": {
      "duplication_rate_max": 0.25,
      "min_pf_reads": 1000000
    },
    "bisulfite_conversion": {
      "enabled": true,
      "source": "auto",
      "min_conversion_rate_pct": 99.0
    },
    "fragmentomics": {
      "enabled": true,
      "profile": "cfdna"
    },
    "cycle_screening": {
      "enabled": true,
      "r2_quality_threshold": 30,
      "max_trim_bases": 8
    }
  }
}

Bisulfite conversion: reads bisulfite_conversion.json sidecar when present; otherwise may use deamination qscore as a qualitative proxy.
cfDNA fragmentomics: when primary_analyte is cfdna, insert-size histogram guardrails can flag abnormal fragment profiles before extraction.

See docs/ANALYTE_PROFILES.md for profile defaults.
crumbs: Part I: Setup and Package Orientation
4  Sample Prep and Quality Control

title: 4  Sample Prep and Quality Control
text:
4.6 Cycle screening and automated recovery
Historically, a single min(mq[20:]) over the combined cycle series could fail fixable Read-2 start dips with a generic “do not proceed” message. Cycle screening (cycle_quality_screening.py) inspects Read 1 and Read 2 separately and assigns a disposition:








Disposition
Meaning
SamplePrep action




USE_CURRENT_ALIGNMENT
Guardrails pass
Continue to extract


REALIGN_TRIM / REALIGN_READ2_TRIM
Fixable read-end quality dip
sample.trim_fastq → Parabricks forceRealign → methyl-qc retry


INVESTIGATE_MULTI_REGION
Multiple low-quality regions
Manual review; no auto-trim


INVESTIGATE_GUARDRAIL_ONLY
Cycles OK; duplication/depth/insert fail
Manual review


NOT_FIXABLE
No automated path
Archive QC-only artifacts, mark failed



Screening writes guardrails.screening with recommended trim bases (trim_front1, trim_tail1, trim_front2, trim_tail2). SamplePrep binds remediateAlignment when disposition is trim-eligible and FASTQs are still on disk.
Important: FASTQs must not be deleted before final alignment QC disposition. The workflow deletes FASTQs only after pass or final reject (including post-remediation retry).
Offline cohort review (no re-align):
source .venv/bin/activate
python scripts/alignment_qc_cohort_screening.py \
  --qc-dir /work/prostate-cancer/alignment_qc \
  --group healthy=/work/prostate-cancer/data/healthy.csv \
  --group pca=/work/prostate-cancer/data/pca.csv \
  --out /work/prostate-cancer/alignment_qc/screening_report
crumbs: Part I: Setup and Package Orientation

title: 4  Sample Prep and Quality Control
section: 4.7 Extraction QC: confirming enough good reads
text:
4.7 Extraction QC: confirming enough good reads
Alignment QC validates the BAM. Extraction QC validates the methylation call layer MethylExtractor produced.

4.7.1 Input: extraction manifest
MethylExtractor writes {sample_id}.extraction_manifest.json with:

summary — genome-wide CpG weighted mean coverage, CHH/CHG methylation levels
per_chromosome — per-chromosome blocks with CG.mean_coverage and related stats



4.7.2 Output: extraction QC JSON
methyl-extraction-qc reads the manifest and writes {sample_id}.extraction_qc.json. Default guardrails (methylextractionqc/guardrails.py):








Guardrail
Default
Interpretation




cpg_weighted_mean_coverage
≥ 10×
Enough reads at CpG sites passing minimum coverage


chh_methylation_level
≤ 0.02
Low non-CpG methylation (conversion sanity) when CHH extracted


chg_methylation_level
≤ 0.02
Same for CHG


chromosome_completeness
all expected chromosomes
Every project chromosome present with CG metrics


chromosome_uniformity
autosomal min/median ≥ 0.5
No severe localized dropout



guardrails.overall_pass maps to workflow extractionQcPass. Failures are terminal today (no automatic retry loop).
Override thresholds via step_config.extraction_qc in the project JSON. Schema: schemas/extraction_qc_output.schema.json.


4.7.3 Why both gates matter







Question
Answered by




Did sequencing and alignment produce a usable BAM?
Alignment QC


Did we extract enough confident methylation signal genome-wide?
Extraction QC



A sample can pass alignment but fail extraction (e.g., coverage collapse on certain chromosomes). Conversely, remediation after alignment QC prevents spending extract GPU time on BAMs that will never support stable downstream statistics.

title: 4  Sample Prep and Quality Control
text:
4.8 Pass, fail, and handoff









Outcome
Alignment QC
Extraction QC
Next step




Pass both
qcPass: true
extractionQcPass: true
Optional full archive → delete FASTQs/BAM → sample ready for DataDrivenPipeline


Fail alignment (not fixable)
qcPass: false
—
QC-only archive, mark failed, skip extract


Fail after remediation
qcPass: false (attempt 2)
—
Same as above


Pass alignment, fail extraction
qcPass: true
extractionQcPass: false
QC-only archive, mark failed; H5 may exist but must not enter production cohorts



When SamplePrep instance COMPLETED, start stability or discovery workflows with the same projectPath. Downstream code resolves HDF5 via methyl_domain.helpers.resolve_methylation_h5_path() — do not hard-code sample paths.
Workers tag scope with MethylSampleRef including alignmentQc, extractionQc, and methylation refs for traceability.

title: 6  Stage: Stability
text:
6.4 Composable workflow profiles
DomainProgram workflows support selectable paths via context profiles in workflow_engine/domain/profiles/. Use methyl-validation run-workflow or methyl-workflow-run with --context-file.
Gene stability without DMP FeatureCuts (discovery DMPs → mapper → enricher → stability on enricher genes):

Profile: gene_enricher_stability.profile.json
Program: mc_gene_enricher_stability.program.json
Set stability_featurecuts_enabled: false, stability_gene_featurecuts_enabled: false, stability_gene_freq as needed
Mapper uses dmps-*-discovery.csv; enricher applies disease filters from step_config.enricher

DMP panel stability (split detector + pipeline.dmp_select): profile dmp_panel_stability or full_biomarker_gene_fc.
Discovery DMPs → broad mapper → gene FeatureCuts (stable gene panel for model): profile discovery_gene_featurecuts with pca1_5_mc_stability.program.json. Mapper uses dmps-*-discovery.csv; pipeline.dmp_select still runs so pipeline.gene_select has classifier DMP exports for validation. Biomarker/PPI pre-filter is off by default (largest gene pool); enable with "runBiomarkerFilter": true in context.
Biomarker / PPI pre-filter (validation.biomarker_filter): optional via ${runBiomarkerFilter}; modes ppi_only, disease_only, disease_and_ppi under step_config.validation or gene_selection. Can run on mapper gene pools without gene FeatureCuts.
See docs/domain_program_language.md for the full profile matrix and IF branch flags (runDmpSelection, runGeneFeaturecuts, …).

title: 6  Stage: Stability
text:

Do not proceed to freeze when stable panel is missing or empty.

11.2 Workflow action observability
Each workflow ACTION executed by methyl-worker submits a typed output_json to the database (validated against schemas/tasks/*.json). Outputs include timing (duration_ms), branch code (result_code), and paths to artifacts on shared storage.
On /work, look for:

Per-action manifests: {output_dir}/.action_results/{action_name}.{run_key}.json — full typed result written by CLIs (e.g. pipeline.dmp_select, pipeline.mapper) or reconstructed by the worker collector.
Sample prep timeline: {sampleDir}/{sampleId}.sample_prep_log.jsonl — append-only JSONL audit for download, align, QC, extract, archive steps.
Validation / MC timeline: {monteCarloRunsRoot}/action_run_log.jsonl — append-only log for validation-category actions (plan, stability, model_mc, etc.).

title: 14  Distributed MethylValidation on shared storage
text:
14.1 Purpose
Run discovery Monte Carlo (and related queue-backed work) on several machines when a single host cannot finish n_iterations in acceptable wall time. Every worker must read and write the same output_base tree (commonly shared NFS under /work/...).
crumbs: 14  Distributed MethylValidation on shared storage

title: 14  Distributed MethylValidation on shared storage
text:
14.2 Prerequisites

One MonteCarloConfig (dedicated mc.json or a project with step_config.validation) with output_base on shared storage
The same virtual environment and methyl-* CLIs on each worker
R/W access to: output_base/<project_name>/monte_carlo_runs/ and the queue/ subtree created by planning
crumbs: 14  Distributed MethylValidation on shared storage

title: 14  Distributed MethylValidation on shared storage
text:
14.3 Layout (under monte_carlo_runs/)







Path
Role




queue/mc_config.json
Snapshotted config for workers


queue/plan_runs.json
Planned runs and task JSON paths


queue/tasks/run_####.json
One task = one run-task invocation


queue/queue_manifest.jsonl / queue/commands.sh
Optional export for a job scheduler


run_####/queue_task_status.json
Worker completion status


run_####/queue_local_step_timings.json
Merged by aggregate-results into step_timings.csv



Full path reference: packages/methylvalidation/docs/DISTRIBUTED_QUEUE.md.
crumbs: 14  Distributed MethylValidation on shared storage

title: 14  Distributed MethylValidation on shared storage
text:
14.4 Command sequence
1) Plan (one process; creates run dirs and task JSON, no heavy steps):
source .venv/bin/activate
methyl-validation plan-runs --config /work/experiments/my_mc_config.json --overwrite
# or:  methyl-validation plan-runs --project /work/prostate-cancer/configs/project_Healthy_vs_PCa1-4-CG.json --overwrite
--overwrite only replaces queue/tasks/ and regenerates the plan; it does not remove existing run_#### output directories. To delete all run_#### trees before planning, add --wipe-runs (irreversible). Without --overwrite, completed runs (see queue_task_status.json + per-run task under queue/tasks/) are not written over; you can add iterations and only the new run_#### work is planned. run-task skips pipeline work for runs already marked completed unless you pass --force.
2) Export (optional; for a central queue broker):
methyl-validation export-queue --config /work/experiments/my_mc_config.json
3) Workers (one job per task; repeat until the queue is empty):
methyl-validation run-task --task /work/prostate-cancer/Healthy_vs_PCa1-4-CG/monte_carlo_runs/queue/tasks/run_0001.json
4) Aggregate (after successful tasks, or to refresh from a partial set):
methyl-validation aggregate-results --config /work/experiments/my_mc_config.json
# add --stability to run the same DMP/gene stability pass as monolithic methyl-validation --stability
If adaptive stop settings are enabled for monolithic stability runs, remember queue workers do not coordinate global early termination on their own. Keep stability_early_stop_enabled=false for queue-first executions unless your scheduler supports coordinator-side cancellation logic.
Legacy: a single process may still run methyl-validation --stability without subcommands; behavior is unchanged.

title: 15  Optional hyperparameter search
text:
15.1 When to use
After a baseline methyl-validation path is understood, use a controlled outer loop to compare candidate settings—typically Tier A knobs in step_config.validation / MonteCarloConfig (e.g. stability_dmp_freq, n_iterations as budget, stability_min_balanced_accuracy). Tuning detector and model backends (Tier B/C) is a separate, often nested exercise; see the theory chapter on multi-stage search tradeoffs in docs/theory/chapters/15-model-creation-and-validation.qmd (Optional pipeline hyperparameter search).

title: 15  Optional hyperparameter search
text:
15.2 What it is

A read-only scalar objective (J) is computed from artifacts under monte_carlo_runs/ (mainly metrics_summary.json, optional stability/stability_summary.json).
The methyl-hyperparam-search entry point is a small grid driver: for each grid point it writes work_dir/trial_NNNN/mc_config.json with a merged MonteCarloConfig and a distinct output_base, runs methyl-validation (e.g. with --stability), then scores the run.
It does not use sklearn.model_selection CV: each evaluation is a subprocess and file read.

Formula and weights: packages/methylvalidation/docs/HYPERPARAMETER_SEARCH.md (full (J), ObjectiveWeights, constraint semantics).

title: 15  Optional hyperparameter search
text:
15.3 Command example
Use a dedicated MC config and a work directory on shared storage if many trials:
source .venv/bin/activate
methyl-hyperparam-search \
  --config /work/experiments/my_mc_config.json \
  --work-dir /work/experiments/hp_run1 \
  --grid '{"stability_dmp_freq": [0.6, 0.7], "stability_min_balanced_accuracy": [null, 0.5]}' \
  -- \
  --stability

JSON null in --grid omits that field so the base config value is kept.
Results: work-dir/search_summary.json (per-trial rows and best feasible trial, if any).
--weights-json can point to a file for ObjectiveWeights.
--baseline-summary /path/to/metrics_summary.json enforces rollout-style feasibility vs a baseline (same idea as methyl-validation --rollout-compare); see packages/methylvalidation/docs/ROLLOUT.md and packages/methylvalidation/docs/HYPERPARAMETER_SEARCH.md.
--dry-run only writes trial configs and paths; no pipeline subprocesses.

title: 15  Optional hyperparameter search
text:
15.4 Pitfalls

Discovery vs calibration: settings that optimize stability panel size may not optimize NLL, Brier, or ECE; prefer a two-stage strategy or tight constraints, not a single ad hoc weight mix.
n_iterations: treat primarily as compute budget to stabilize medians, not a dimension to grid-search widely without cost awareness.
